_about: Hand-built SEED subset of the 2023 AGS Beers Criteria, summarized in our own words (the criteria are copyrighted; never paste table text here). Owner: B. Before the demo, check every entry against the paper and set verified=true. Drug names are lower-case generic ingredient names.

source.title: American Geriatrics Society 2023 updated AGS Beers Criteria for potentially inappropriate medication use in older adults

drugs.label: Older-style (first-generation) antihistamines, often in night-time sleep aids
drugs.risk: Strongly anticholinergic: can cause confusion, dry mouth, constipation and falls; the body gets used to them as a sleep aid.
drugs.advice: Ask about a non-drowsy allergy medicine or other ways to improve sleep.

drugs.label: Benzodiazepines (anxiety or sleep medicines)
drugs.risk: Raise the risk of memory problems, confusion, falls, broken bones and car crashes.
drugs.advice: Do not stop suddenly; ask about a plan to lower or replace it.

drugs.label: Z-drug sleeping pills
drugs.risk: Similar risks to benzodiazepines (confusion, falls, fractures) with little extra sleep.
drugs.advice: Ask about other ways to improve sleep.

drugs.label: Common anti-inflammatory pain relievers (NSAIDs)
drugs.risk: Regular use raises the risk of stomach bleeding and ulcers and can strain the kidneys.
drugs.advice: Avoid regular use unless other options do not work; ask about stomach protection.

drugs.label: Daily aspirin taken to prevent a first heart attack or stroke
drugs.risk: For people without heart disease, the bleeding risk can outweigh the benefit when started at an older age.
drugs.advice: If you take aspirin daily, ask whether you still need it.

drugs.label: Sulfonylurea diabetes pills
drugs.risk: Can cause dangerously low blood sugar.
drugs.advice: Ask whether a diabetes medicine with lower low-blood-sugar risk fits you.

drugs.label: Muscle relaxants
drugs.risk: Cause drowsiness and anticholinergic effects and raise fall risk; benefit at safe doses is doubtful.
drugs.advice: Ask about other options for muscle pain.

drugs.label: Stomach-acid reducers (proton pump inhibitors) taken longer than 8 weeks
drugs.risk: Long-term use is linked to gut infections, bone loss and fractures.
drugs.advice: If you have taken it for more than 8 weeks, ask whether you still need it.

drugs.label: Warfarin started as a first choice blood thinner
drugs.risk: Has a higher bleeding risk than newer blood thinners for many people.
drugs.advice: Do not stop it on your own; ask whether a newer option suits you.

drugs.label: Older antidepressants and paroxetine
drugs.risk: Strongly anticholinergic and sedating: confusion, constipation, dizziness when standing.
drugs.advice: Do not stop suddenly; ask about alternatives.

drugs.label: Overactive-bladder pills (antimuscarinics)
drugs.risk: Strongly anticholinergic: can worsen memory and cause constipation and dry mouth.
drugs.advice: Ask about bladder training or an option with fewer side effects.

drugs.label: Metoclopramide (nausea / stomach emptying)
drugs.risk: Can cause movement problems, some of which may not go away.
drugs.advice: Ask whether you still need it.

drugs.label: Meperidine (opioid pain reliever)
drugs.risk: Can cause confusion and seizures at usual doses.
drugs.advice: Ask about a safer pain reliever.

drugs.label: Megestrol (appetite stimulant)
drugs.risk: Raises the risk of blood clots with little benefit for weight.
drugs.advice: Ask whether you still need it.

drugs.label: Mineral oil taken by mouth (laxative)
drugs.risk: Can be breathed into the lungs by accident.

combos.label: Two or more anticholinergic medicines
combos.risk: Effects add up and raise the risk of memory problems, confusion and falls.
combos.advice: Ask whether one of them can be stopped or replaced.

combos.label: Three or more medicines that act on the brain
combos.risk: Together they raise the risk of falls and broken bones.
combos.advice: Ask for a review of which ones are still needed.

combos.label: Opioid pain reliever + benzodiazepine
combos.risk: Together they can slow breathing and raise overdose risk.
combos.advice: Talk to your doctor soon about this combination.

combos.label: Opioid pain reliever + gabapentin or pregabalin
combos.risk: Together they can cause heavy sleepiness and slowed breathing.
combos.advice: Ask whether this combination is still needed.

combos.label: Warfarin + certain antibiotics
combos.risk: These antibiotics can make warfarin much stronger and raise bleeding risk.
combos.advice: Tell whoever prescribed the antibiotic that you take warfarin.
